name: Port Moresby Nature Park
note: Wildlife and botanical park (formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens) with tree kangaroos, cassowaries, birds of paradise, a WWII walk-through aviary and gardens.

facts.fact: 30-acre wildlife and botanical park on Goro Kaeage Road with over 500 animals; attractions include a WWII walk-through aviary, tree kangaroo trail, Reptile Haus, cassowary corridor and bird of paradise precinct
Formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens; the adjoining National Orchid Garden is a separate site

2026 fee brochure: operating hours 9 am - 4 pm every day; entry for tourists K22 adult, K17 student with ID, K12 child 3-12; local residents K12 adult; guided tour K66 for a group of 1-4 people (K15 for 5 or more) on top of entry

access_note: In Port Moresby on Goro Kaeage Road between the University of PNG and Port Moresby National High School; arrange transport through a hotel (taxis rarely metered, agree price).

name: National Museum and Art Gallery
note: Museum: PNG's national museum in Waigani, with carvings, beads, traditional boats, cultural objects and WWII relics outside.

facts.fact: National museum in Waigani on Independence Drive next to the National Parliament, with sculptures, beads, traditional boats and cultural objects
Photography not permitted inside; newer objects and WWII remains (planes, tanks) sit outside

note: Island: a private island resort in Bootless Inlet, 20-30 minutes by boat from Port Moresby, with snorkelling, diving, kayaks and day visits.

facts.fact: Private island resort in Bootless Bay; day passes give access to private beaches, pools and restaurants; round-trip ferry from Tahira terminal included

name: Mount Wilhelm
note: Mountain: Papua New Guinea's highest peak (4,509 m), climbed by guided treks from Keglsugl (Simbu) or Ambullua (Western Highlands).

facts.fact: PNG's highest mountain at 4,509 m; the tourism authority says it is accessible but not easy and guides should always be taken; good road to Keglsugl village from Kundiawa, with huts and lodges at the base
Base camp Keglsugl is about five hours by road from Goroka; the climb involves an overnight stay on the mountain; local guide is essential; temperatures below freezing at the summit
Operator packages (e.g. an Ambullua-route traverse) start around AUD 3,799 per person, bundling permits, community fees and guides

note: Island: Buka Island, the arrival point for Bougainville by air and the Buka Passage boat trips; the island has the airport, the tourist office and most places to stay.

Air Niugini flies Port Moresby to Buka daily except Sunday; a short water taxi crosses to the main island; a gravelled road circles Buka Island

name: Sohano Island
note: Island: Sohano, the most visited island in the Buka Passage, with simple eateries and places to stay, a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on its northern tip and a short K2 boat ride from Buka.

facts.text: Sohano is a 10-minute boat trip across the Buka Passage from the harbour beside Buka Market; it was the provincial capital for several decades after WWII.
Walking the island you find a large traditional mona canoe, an ANZAC memorial to fallen soldiers, old trees and views across the passage.
Wikivoyage describes a Japanese war memorial and plane wreck on the northern tip, and Tchibo Rock, said by local legend to have magical properties.
Commuter boats cost about K2: go to the beach and ask the drivers who is leaving next. Simple eateries and places to stay are on the island.
Bougainville EcoVentures runs a guided walking tour of Sohano.

access_note: Short boat hop from Buka town; no guide needed.
unverified: No fixed opening hours; boat fare K2 is from an older guide and not confirmed as current

name: Mount Balbi
note: Mountain: Mount Balbi (2,715 m), an active volcano in the Emperor Range, the highest in the Bougainville chain, reached by a three-day trek from Wakunai.

facts.text: Mount Balbi (local name Tutue) is the highest point on Bougainville at 2,715 m; the trek climbs a steep track through varying forest types.
Near the summit are sulphur vents, a turquoise blue lake and steaming hot springs; the volcano is classed as active but has not erupted in historic time.
The usual route is a three-day hike started from Wakunai on the east coast, where guides are available; one trekker reports over 20 hours of walking across three nights.
Treks cross private land, so a local guide is essential; local operators include Rotokas Ecotourism (Wakunai) and Bougainville Experience Tours (Arawa).
An extension across the Emperor Range to the west coast takes about a week.

access_note: Remote; reached by road to Wakunai then on foot. Guide required (private land). Track access has reportedly been closed at times over landowner disputes; check with a tour operator before planning.
unverified: No guide or landowner fee published
No fixed hours

name: Nissan Island
note: Island: Nissan (Green Island), about 100 km north of Buka, with an American WWII airstrip, relics and a guest house with no telephone booking.

facts.text: The Green Islands, commonly called the Nissan Islands, lie about 94 km north-west of Buka Island and are reached by about a four-hour boat ride from Buka Town.
Nissan is a crescent enclosing a turquoise lagoon, ringed by coral reefs; visitors are welcomed with a traditional ceremony.

WWII relics include the Allied-built airstrip and island road, and the concrete bases of a supply warehouse and water reservoir known as Nixon's swimming pool, where Richard Nixon served as a supply officer; some unexploded bombs remain live.
Dudualen Beach at Balil Village on the northern tip is described as good for snorkelling and diving.
There are three guesthouses on the island that cannot be booked ahead because there is no phone service, and they receive very few guests.
Travel on a boat registered with the National Maritime Safety Authority and check the weather service first.

access_note: Remote; boat only (about 4 hours from Buka). No phone booking for guesthouses.

name: Samarai
note: Island: former colonial capital and trading port at the entrance to Milne Bay, a 20-minute walk round, with ruins of its boom-town past and a National Historical Heritage Island listing; reached by boat from Alotau.

facts.text: Samarai is a 59-acre island at the entrance to Milne Bay that was once an important stopover between Australia and East Asia; in 1902 it exported three times as much by value as Port Moresby.
Little remains of the town because it was destroyed in WWII; the island was declared a National Historical Heritage Island in 2006.
It takes about 20 minutes to walk around the island.
Public dinghies reportedly leave from Sanderson Bay in Alotau, usually in the afternoon, and return the next morning; one traveller paid 50 kina return and the trip took over three hours.
The provincial tourism page lists Samarai as a historic colonial-era port with preserved architecture and a popular island-hopping stop.

access_note: Boat only from Alotau; schedule informal.

name: Tawali
note: Dive site: reef and drop-offs at Tawali on the coast near Alotau, named by the PNG tourism authority as a world-renowned Milne Bay dive site; reached by boat, with the Tawali Leisure and Dive Resort on the bluff above.

facts.text: Tawali is a rainforest headland with a fringing reef, reached only by sea; the resort has run since 1994 and offers more than 60 dive sites within an hour.
Dives include coral gardens, walls, wrecks, muck diving and the only underwater post box in Papua New Guinea.

The resort's own 2026 tour rates range from US$35-60 per person for the skull caves and waterfall walk, to US$48-75 for coral garden snorkelling (price falls with group size); dive packages start at US$2,900 for seven nights with 15 dives.
The national tourism authority names Tawali, Deacon's Reef, Wahoo Point and Gonubalabala as world-renowned Milne Bay dive sites.

access_note: Boat transfer from Alotau; stays are by resort package. Rainforest bird walks leave at 4:00 AM.

name: Fergusson Island
note: Island: geothermal volcanic island reached only by boat, with trekking trails and birdwatching for a rare bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode; its hot springs at Deidei are listed separately.

facts.text: Fergusson is the largest of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands (1,437 sq km), mostly mountainous rainforest with three large volcanoes.
Wikivoyage calls it a geothermal island with good birdwatching, including a rare species of bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode, reached only by boat.
The D'Entrecasteaux islands still show volcanic activity, especially around Dobu and Fergusson.

name: Trobriand Islands
note: Island group: the Kiriwina Islands, raised coral atolls in the north of Milne Bay known as the Islands of Love, with yam-harvest dancing, village stays, the Kula ring and white beaches; reached by a twice-weekly PNG Air flight from Alotau.

facts.text: The Trobriand (Kiriwina) Islands are raised coral atolls in northern Milne Bay with white-sand beaches, coral lagoons and rainforest; about 12,000 people live mostly on Kiriwina.

The culture is matrilineal and centred on yam cultivation; a distinct version of cricket introduced by missionaries is played, and traditional dancing is preserved, especially during the yam harvest in June or July.
The islands are part of the Kula Ring exchange network.
PNG Air flies twice weekly from Port Moresby via Alotau on a Twin Otter; Air Niugini no longer flies there. Lodges include Kiriwina Lodge and Butia Lodge.

access_note: Remote; twice-weekly small-plane flight. Basic lodges.

name: Louisiade Archipelago
note: Archipelago: about 100 islands in the far southeast of Milne Bay, a diver's paradise and yachting destination with coral reefs; few visitors and reached mainly by private yacht, so a region rather than a single stop.

facts.text: The Louisiade Archipelago is ten larger volcanic islands and about 90 smaller coral islands, many fringed by reefs.
It is renowned for coral reefs and diving and receives very few tourists apart from passing yachts; it is difficult to reach.
Communities live a subsistence life and almost everything is privately owned, so ask permission before fishing or taking anything; trading goods with canoes is common.
Islands include Misima, the Deboyne Islands, Calvados Chain, Duchateau group, Sudest and Rossel.

access_note: Remote; reached mainly by private yacht, charter or liveaboard; Misima has a flight.
unverified: No fee or hours published

name: Misima Island
note: Island: the most populated and most accessible Louisiade island, served by air to Bwagaoia with a guest house; a closed gold mine and island-hopping stop named by the PNG tourism authority.

facts.text: Misima is the most populated and most accessible island of the Louisiade Archipelago, with about 5,000 people.
A gold mine opened in 1990 briefly changed island life and closed in 2004.
Airlines PNG connects Alotau with Misima twice weekly (per Wikivoyage); the tourism authority lists Misima among the popular island-hopping stops with quiet beaches.
The provincial tourism page names Misima as known for natural beauty and quiet beaches.
